- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often overestimates near-term upside — reduce forecast slope or cap upward movement.  
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) after spikes — apply downward bias to first 5 days if recent price surged.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — if price is above 85–90, forecast should not rise beyond 95–98 unless sentiment strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33 or 0.20 spikes, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope or add 1–2% downward adjustment.  
- Model underestimates true volatility in 30-day horizon — if true outcome shows >10% swings, adjust forecast to reflect higher variance (e.g., ±2–3% buffer).
